packing: per shot c0..c(n-1), c0 = rightmost char; shots concatenated in returned order; MSB-first; partial byte dropped

channel_rule.why: 0.9 at 4096 shots fails 40/156 healthy-but-biased qubits (margin 0.020 alone costs 0.057 bit) = false red; 0.5 names a channel broken only when max(p0,p1) exceeds 0.707 after the 99 % margin - on r0 that is exactly the qubit whose vendor readout error (0.33) explains it; biased-but-usable channels are charged in the accounting instead

predictions.K3: fraction of ones over all bits in [0.4, 0.6]
predictions.K4: buyer checker (qrng_fuggetlen) PASS, accounting and exclusion recomputed
predictions.K5: excluded channels (h_99 < 0.5 bit/bit) between 0 and 4; r0 under the same rule: [[72, 0.2769, 0.4322, 0.3345]]
predictions.K6: per-channel accounting h_acc in [6.731, 8.0] bits per sample (r0: 7.230826)

interpretation: K1-K6 pass = the module's per-channel rule, fixed before the data, runs end to end on a real quantum source without the r0 false red, and a broken channel costs output, not the block. K7 is the new physics-side claim: the per-qubit bias is a stable device property, not noise. Statistics still cannot certify quantumness; the receipt stays 'statistical'. A failure is reported as measured.
